obstacle_physical_radius.contract: runtime serial 55 (45912b9d): each registered obstacle is {x, y, r, rp}. `r` is the keep-out corridor the steering dodge uses and is UNCHANGED here (the handoff spells it r_keepout; the scenario package already maps r_keepout -> r). `rp` is the solid's physical radius the pin reflex uses; it is optional and defaults to `r`. The runtime refuses the WHOLE registration call unless every rp is finite, >= 0.1 and <= its own r.

coverage_caveat.applies_to: the deck flanks and ramp flanks
coverage_caveat.options_for_the_runtime: (a) accept the gap -- the reflex is a proximity trigger, and under-arming mid-face is the pre-G12 behaviour rather than a new regression; (b) use point-to-SEGMENT distance for these (the segment primitive the runtime worker raised in round 7 and withdrew -- G12's 10 handle contacts re-motivate it); (c) ask geometry for denser face samples. Do NOT substitute a fat circle: that is the 9.4 m disc that caused the defect
coverage_caveat.superseded_by: obstacle_face_coverage (A25, v3.6) audits EVERY face against the reflex's measured arming half-span. This block keeps the flank numbers; the deck NOSE it used to omit is now sampled and covered.
coverage_caveat.why: a circle cannot represent a wall. A zero-radius disc arms correctly for a car on the perpendicular through a sample and not at all for a car touching the face midway between two samples

floor_deviation.why: their true physical radius is 0.0 -- the registered point lies ON the solid's surface -- but the runtime refuses rp < 0.1, so 0.1 is the smallest expressible value. Effect: the arming disc for these points is ~2.6 m instead of ~2.5 m at a 2.5 m car reach, a 0.1 m over-statement. The alternative -- omitting rp -- defaults them to r = 6.5/8.0 m, which is the 9.4 m disc this round exists to remove. Recorded, not silent.

kind_meanings.batter: jamb mid/outer-face points, which sit INSIDE the battered jamb's plan footprint at mid-slope; the 1:1 batter reaches h/2 from the point to its toe, so rp = h/2 measured from batter_top() at that station
kind_meanings.corner: the registered point IS the solid's extremity (deck nose/rear corners; the spout jamb noses, where the batter has zero height at r 76). The measured physical radius is 0.0 and contact happens when the car body reaches the point -- emitted at the 0.1 floor, see floor_deviation
kind_meanings.face: a sample standing ON a long flat face (deck flanks, ramp inner flanks). The surface passes through the point, so the measured radius is 0.0: exact on the perpendicular through that sample, and it OVER-estimates the gap between samples -- see coverage_caveat. Emitted at the 0.1 floor
kind_meanings.post: a whole convex solid registered at its axis/centre; rp is a true circumscribed plan radius and the disc IS the obstacle (masher 1.2 and grinder 1.5 are the cylinder radii; the geyser tower is a 3x3 m BOX, touchable at its corner, so 1.5*sqrt(2) = 2.121 -- which is the ~2.1 the gates measured, not the 1.5 half-width)

obstacle_physical_radius.pass_through: emit ONLY {x, y, r, rp} to hotPotatoRegisterObstacles. `rp_kind` is authoring metadata for the record and must not be passed through. hotPotatoGetObstacles() echoes rp, so the package can assert what actually landed.
obstacle_physical_radius.rp_le_r_check: PASS -- no obstacle class needs an rp larger than its own r; the worst ratio is the jamb mid-face at 2.321 / 8.0 = 0.29. Asserted per point by A24, which FAILS the build rather than clamping.
obstacle_physical_radius.semantics: maximum plan half-extent of the solid about the registered point -- 'how far from this point can the solid still be touched'. Feeds the unpin reflex's envelope (gap = |car - post| - rp - car_reach).

shape_junctions.rule: relief measured ACROSS a junction between two shapes on a drivable surface, capped at RELIEF_CAP (0.020 m). Authored rebates and lifts are measured, not excused.
shape_junctions.why: every earlier relief assert ran WITHIN one shape; nothing measured the step a car actually crosses. v3.6's 145 mm deck-rear claim came from an audit that ASSUMED the edge was a straight chord -- this assert reads the authored vertices and measures 0.005 mm.
